title: [YouPass Collect] - Australian Expenditure Across Categories in 1986 and 2009
prompt: The table below illustrates the percentage of expenditure allocated to 11 different categories per capita in Australia in 1986 and 2009. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table illustrates the proportion of per capita spending across 11 different categories in Australia in 1986 and 2009.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the majority of expenditure categories experienced an increase over 23 years, with only three categories witnessing a decline. Additionally, housing consistently accounted for the largest share of spending in both years.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Starting with the major expenditure categories, housing represented 22% of total spending in 1986, which was 4% higher than food and 8% higher than transport. By 2009, the proportion allocated to housing had risen to 26%, solidifying its position as the most significant expenditure item. In contrast, the percentage spent on food decreased to 15%, while transport saw a marginal decline to 13% by the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Regarding the remaining categories, recreation and entertainment, and other goods and services each accounted for 8% in 1986, while electricity and water stood at 7%. Meanwhile, clothing, healthcare, and insurance and financial services ranged from 5% to 6%, whereas education and communication represented the smallest shares, at 4% and 3% respectively. Over the following two decades, communication expenditure doubled to 6%, while healthcare and utilities (electricity and water) both increased by 3 percentage points each, reaching 8% and 10% respectively. Recreation also rose to 10%, and education and insurance grew more modestly to 6% and 7% in that order. Meanwhile, clothing was the only category in this group to decline, falling to 4%, while other goods and services increased slightly to 9%.
